_meta.description: Pre-written cluster impressions for the 2D flavor map (UMAP + DBSCAN).
_meta.note: Regenerate after adding/removing bottles. Auto-generation kicks in for unmatched clusters.

0.impression: Extreme botanicals · Four bottles with nothing in common on the label, everything in common in the glass. Alpine herbs, damask rose, Chios mastic and 90% anise — all intensely aromatic, all transformative in small doses. Use any of these and the drink knows it.

1.impression: Italian bitter · The backbone of aperitivo culture. Twelve bottles spanning the full spectrum from Campari’s citrus-bitter to Cynar’s earthy artichoke to Angostura’s aromatic spice. The largest cluster in the collection — because this is what the bar is built around.

bottles: Weller Special Reserve Single Barrel Select
Elmer T. Lee Single Barrel Sour Mash
2.impression: American whiskey · Eleven bourbons in tight formation — vanilla, oak and caramel with varying wheat-rye balance. The most internally coherent cluster in the collection. Small differences matter here: the wheated bottles sit slightly apart from the high-rye mashbills.

3.impression: Structured complexity · The collection’s most unexpected pairing. A Virginia small-batch bourbon and an apple-brandy-based sweet vermouth from the same state — separated by category, united by structured caramel, body and a shared unhurried weight. A reminder that flavor doesn’t respect labels.

4.impression: Core gin · Citrus, floral and botanical — the gin cluster without the outliers. Tanqueray anchors the citrus pole, the three Japanese gins bring floral lift and a softer juniper presence. All four work in any classic gin cocktail.

5.impression: Japanese sake · Two bottles, one quiet corner of the collection. Low intensity, delicate umami, subtle fruit. Nothing else in the bar competes for this flavor space — which is exactly why they cluster alone.

Aperol.impression: Between worlds · Too light and orange-sweet for the bitter cluster, too amaro-tinged for the gin cluster. Aperol Spritz works because Aperol needs Prosecco to find its place — in pure flavor space it stands alone.

Koval__Thresh & Winnow Foret.label: Thresh & Winnow Foret
Koval__Thresh & Winnow Foret.impression: Forest outlier · The most botanical gin in the collection by far. Close to the extreme botanicals cluster (Braulio, Mastiha) but too gin-structured to fully merge. A bridge between two worlds that belongs to neither.

Metaxa__3 Stars.label: 3 Stars
Metaxa__3 Stars.impression: Greek brandy island · Muscat wine base plus Mediterranean herbs creates a profile with no close neighbor. Fruity enough to drift toward gin, structured enough to drift toward bourbon — but not close enough to either.

Pilla__Select Aperitivo.label: Select Aperitivo
Pilla__Select Aperitivo.impression: Venetian aperitivo bridge · Select sits between the gin cluster and the bitter cluster, sharing botanical character with the former and bitter-citrus with the latter. The original Spritz ingredient that predates Aperol — and more complex than either cluster captures.

Godo Shusei__Oshuku Umeshu (Ohshukubai S.label: Oshuku Umeshu (Ohshukubai Shigoku Nidan)
Godo Shusei__Oshuku Umeshu (Ohshukubai S.impression: Plum solitude · Double-macerated ume plums produce an extreme sweet-tart profile unlike anything else in the collection. Too fruity-acidic for sake cluster, too sweet for anywhere else. Nearest neighbor is Dassai 45, but the distance is significant.

Martini__Riserva Speciale Ambrato.label: Riserva Speciale Ambrato
Martini__Riserva Speciale Ambrato.impression: Amber bridge · Sits between the gin botanical cluster and the vermouth territory. Its amber-honey-chamomile profile is too distinctive to merge with either — a vermouth that behaves like a liqueur.

Carpano__Antica Formula.label: Antica Formula
Carpano__Antica Formula.impression: Noble outlier · The most structured vermouth in the collection gravitates toward the bourbon cluster on vanilla and body, but its bitter complexity keeps it from fully joining. Lives at the intersection of two worlds — which is why it makes both a Manhattan and a Negroni exceptional.

Martini__Vermouth Rosso.label: Vermouth Rosso
Martini__Vermouth Rosso.impression: Entry-point vermouth · Light enough to drift toward the gin cluster, amaro-adjacent enough to brush the bitter cluster. The most ‘average’ vermouth in the collection — versatile precisely because it commits to nothing extreme.
